full_judgment:
This Rule by the plaintiffs directed against Order dated 19-2-1987 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 114 of 2983 affirming order No. 35 dated 4-9-1982 passed by the learned Munsif, 6th Court, Dhaka allowing Miscellaneous Case No. 65 of 1982 under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure arising out of Title Suit No. 211 of 1978 of the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka renumbered as Title Suit No. 933 of 1982 of the Court of Munsif, 6th Court, Dhaka. 

 2. Plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for ejectment of ordinary ejectable monthly tenants at will stating that plaintiffs are the sole 16 annas owner of Municipal Holding No. 64, Purana Paltan, within PS Lalbagh now Motijheel, Dhaka. The defendants have been inducted by the plaintiffs as monthly tenants-at-will at a rent of Taka 320 per month payable according to English Calendar in respect of one pucca ground floor room No.3 of the building lying and situated at Rezia Manzil, 64, Purana Paltan in which defendants are carrying on business therein under the name and style 'Continental Motors'. As per agreement of tenancy dated 15-4-69 the rent of the month concerned of the suit room shall be paid within 7 days of following next  month. Defendants are always irregular in making payment of monthly rent and stopped payment of rent for the period of January, 1975 to December, 1977 totaling Taka 11,520. In further case of the plaintiffs that without the knowledge and consent of the plaintiffs the defendants have allowed others to display their sign board over the tenanted suit room. The suit room is now bonafide required by the plain- tiff for personal use and occupation to accommodate their family members. Plaintiffs through their Advocate issued notice dated 4-1-77 under section 106 of the Transfer of property Act under registered post with A/D to the defendants asking them to quit and vacate the suit room with the expiry of 31st day of January, 1977. But the defendants did not pay any heed to the aforesaid notice and did not vacate the suit room within the time fixed in the notice. The defendants with malafide motive did not receive the aforesaid notice dated 4-1-77 which was returned to the plaintiffs with the remark 'refused' as per postal endorsement dated 6-1-77, thereafter plaintiffs filed the suit. 

 3. In the suit, as it appears from the order sheets that defendant did not appear and the suit was posted for exparte disposal and the suit was decreed exparte on 12-9-78. After exparte decree, plaintiff put the decree into execution and Court issued writ of delivery of possession on 30-9-80; defendants were evicted from the suit premises on 5-10-80. Thereafter, defendants filed application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka, which is registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 192 of 1980. In the said miscellaneous case plaintiff entered appearance after service return. On 30-10-1981 said miscellaneous case as per notification No. 26-J-IV /50C-9/78 dated 14-1-81 was transferred to the Court of Munsif 6th Court, Dhaka. learned Munsif received the case record on 22-4-1982 and registered the miscellaneous case as Miscellaneous Case No. 65 of 1982. Learned Munsif on 4-9-82 allowed the miscellaneous case exparte and after vacating the order of exparte decree, registered the suit to its original file and number as Title Suit No. 9333 of 1982. The petitioners thereafter moved before the learned Munsif as well as revisional Court for setting aside the ex parte order registering the suit to its file and number. Thereafter, petitioners moved this Court and obtained this rule. Defendant opposite parties appeared in the rule, filed counter affidavit but at any point of time defendant-opposite parties did not appear before this Court. In the counter-affidavit defendant-opposite parties denied the plaint case of the petitioners. 

 4. Mr Fida M Kamal, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners, submits that, learned judges of both the Courts below did not consider that the miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed long after 2 years 1 month 21 days after the exparte decree and allowed miscellaneous case exparte without considering the delay is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate on reference to section 24A (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that, as per section 24A (2) of the Code, Court is bound to inform the parties as to transfer of the case and in absence of any notice to the parties informing the transfer, Court has no jurisdiction to pass any order on the case/suit. Learned advocate cited the decision of Abdul Khaleque vs Abdul Barek Howlader, 2 BLC 276 and also the Appellate Division of this case of Abdul Khaleque vs Abdul Barek Howlader, reported in 3 BLC (AD) 174 and another decision i.e. the case of Muhammad lshaque vs Abdul Haque, reported in PLD (Karachi) 899. In these decisions the question arises whether transfer Court without satisfying as to service of notice upon the parties can pass the decree exparte. It is admitted position that defendants are out of possession, as such, whether defendants can maintain the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit after setting aside the said decree passed exparte without any prayer for recovery of possession. 

 6. Small Cause Courts constituted under section 5 of Small Causes Courts Act; section 15 of the Act gives jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes i.e. the Court has jurisdiction in the case of eviction of the tenant and Small Causes Courts cannot decide title of any party, it has no jurisdiction to pass the decree for recovery of possession if the tenant thrown out of possession of the premises. It can settle only the rightly of the tenant as regard possession over the suit premises i.e. whether he landlord acted in accordance with law or in accordance of the terms of the agreement, that is, if the rents illegally enhanced, if the land lord curtail the facilities provided under tenancy agreement of the tenant or if the landlord disturbed the tenant in any manner, then Small Causes Court has jurisdiction to look into the matter but Small Causes Courts cannot restored to possession of any tenant dispossessed or thrown out of suit premises by execution of decree. In the instant case as I find by execution of decree defendants were thrown out of the suit premises and when the Miscellaneous case was filed, tenants were out of possession that means, decree of the suit or for the purpose the suit was filed has been satisfied and jurisdiction of Small Causes Courts has been totally ousted as a tenant cannot fight any legal battle if he she is out of possession as Court cannot compelled the land lord to restore possession of an unwanted tenant. And in that case, defendants can seek for damage not for restoration of possession or restoration of the suit. 

 8. Learned Advocate relied on the decisions of Abdul Khaleque vs Abdul Barek Howlader, 3 BLC (AD) 174 wherein it is held that the High Court Division on the ground of following the provision of law as required under section 24A(2) of the Code sent back the case on remand after setting aside the decree of the appellate Court. Leave to appeal was sought from the said judgment on the ground of maintainability of the suit which having not been raised before the revisional Court, it is not open to him now to argue on the merit of the case. 

 9. As per section 24A (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure transfer Court is required to pass order of transfer on a date fixed for the appearance of the parties, and such Court shall communicate the order to such parties direct them to appear before the Court to which the proceeding is transferred. As per provision of section 24A(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure I do not find from the order sheets that order of transfer was made on a Date when the case was fixed for appearance. Such requirement of law would have been duly complied with if the transferee Court would informed the parties of the transfer. But on record there is nothing to show that petitioners were informed about the transfer of the case either by the transferor Court or by the transferee Court. Further, the transferee Court did not pass any order indicating or showing that the petitioners were duly informed about the transfer. 

 10. As per provision of section 24A(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure I do not find from the order sheets transferee Court after receiving the record informed the parties to the case. So these orders passed by the Courts below are bad on this count. 

 11. On the question of limitation, it appears from the record that application filed by the defendants under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure after the period of limitation. I personally checked the application filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and find no explanation as to delay caused in filing the application, which is required to be filed within 30 days and if it is not within that period then there must by some satisfactory explanation explaining the delay in filing the application, present in the application. Learned Judges of the Courts below must have to go through the case record between lines but I find that they did not. Moreover, it appears that the suit was filed in 1987 and also from record it appears that defendants were evicted from the suit premises on 5-11-1980 and it is now more than 31 years, defendants are out of possession, as such, in no imagination defendants can be restored to possession as by this time much water flows in the river Buriganga and such position as I see accepted by plaintiffs and defendants by their conduct. 

 15. The judgment and order dated 19-2- 1987 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 114 of 1983 dismissing the Civil Revision against Order No. 35 dated 4-9-1982 passed by the learned Munsif, 6th Court, Dhaka allowing the Miscellaneous Case No. 65 of 982, original Miscellaneous case No. 192 of 1980 are set aside.
